summary: The study investigates the effect of temperature on the phase formation of titanium dioxide layers on silica surfaces using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The process involves the chemical modification of silica matrices through successive stages of molecular layering, including heat treatment, chemisorption, removal of excess halide, hydrolysis, and drying. The temperature conditions at each stage significantly influence the phase composition and crystalline structure of the titanium dioxide layer, with different temperature ranges leading to the formation of anatase and rutile phases.
evidence: The processes of chemical modification of the surface of solid-phase matrices are widely applied in micro- and nanoelectronics and in the technology of ceramic and composite materials. In this study, the effect of temperature on the chemical composition and character of the phase formation at different stages of ML was determined for the example of the synthesis of a titanium dioxide layer on the surface of dispersed silica.
